bull.b: Sustained gross margins near the high 70s and a ~21% EBIT margin indicate durable pricing power and strong product mix in implantable devices and consumables. This margin base supports reinvestment in R&D and commercialization while cushioning cyclical procedure volume swings over years.

Extremely low leverage and nearly $3B in cash give Edwards financial flexibility for share buybacks, targeted M&A, or elevated R&D spend without stressing liquidity. This buffer supports multi-year product launches and weathering reimbursement or procedure-volume variability.

Rapid TMTT growth and multiple regulatory/clinical milestones diversify revenue beyond TAVR. New device approvals and strong durability data expand addressable markets (mitral/tricuspid and surgical), underpinning a multi-year structural growth runway and reducing single-product concentration risk.

bear.b: A history of revenue dips and variable operating/free cash flow signals sensitivity to procedure volumes, hospital purchasing cycles and working-capital timing. That variability complicates long-range planning for capex, buybacks and R&D allocation, raising execution risk through cycles.

Medicare coverage decisions and pivotal trial outcomes materially affect the addressable patient pool for TAVR/TMTT. Delay or unfavorable results would slow adoption, limit procedure volumes and constrain long-term revenue growth, making policy and clinical readouts structural growth levers.

Increased SG&A spending reduces operating leverage and could compress margins if revenue ramps slower than planned. Higher effective tax and limits on R&D credits depress GAAP profitability, reducing retained earnings and free cash flow available for strategic initiatives over multiple years.
